2608.04144.title: Neighborhood-Aware Dual Biomedical Entity Linking
2608.04144.paper_summary: Biomedical entity linking grounds mentions in clinical and scientific text to entities in a curated knowledge base (KB) with ontological structure, which supports downstream applications such as literature-scale information extraction and patient-record normalization. The task has several challenges at once: the KB contains large numbers of entities, mentions are often ambiguous, and gold labels follow annotation conventions specific to each corpus. To address these challenges, we propose PILOT, a three-stage framework made up of neighborhood-aware retrieval, dual reranking, and score fusion. The retriever injects ontological structure from both the query and KB side, by reformulating mentions and pooling entity embeddings. The retrieved pool is then scored from two complementary views, one over surface forms and one over context, and fused together. PILOT achieves the state of the art on average across five widely-used benchmarks and remains efficient at inference.
2608.04144.paper_summary_zh: 生物醫學實體連結將臨床和科學文本中的提及與具有本體結構的策劃知識庫（KB）中的實體對應，這支持下游應用，如文獻規模的信息提取和病歷標準化。這項任務同時面臨幾個挑戰：知識庫包含大量實體，提及通常模糊不清，且金標籤遵循特定於每個語料庫的註釋規範。為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出了PILOT，一個由鄰域感知檢索、雙重重排序和分數融合組成的三階段框架。檢索器通過重新表述提及和聚合實體嵌入，從查詢和知識庫兩側注入本體結構。然後，檢索到的池子從兩個互補的視角進行評分，一個是基於表面形式，另一個是基於上下文，並將其融合在一起。PILOT在五個廣泛使用的基準測試中平均達到最先進的水平，並在推理時保持高效。
